name: Drought
value: Sudan main-season crops failed; no famine call
summary: Crop Monitor rates Sudan's main-season crops a failure after a record-dry season; no major exporter's harvest has failed
state: The GEOGLAM Crop Monitor of 5 Nov says parts of Sudan, South Sudan, Uganda, Kenya and Ethiopia had their driest June–September season on record, rates Sudan's main-season crops a failure and flags poor harvests in Ethiopia, Kenya, Chad and Central America. It gives a 50–80% chance of below-normal rain in southern Africa from November to March with the strong El Niño, though South Africa's ample maize stocks cushion the risk (Daily Maverick, 2 Nov). No drought-driven famine declaration or major exporter's harvest failure was found by 24 Nov, so Watch holds.
for_you: Drought is cutting harvests in East Africa, the Sahel and Central America, where households already face high food prices. Southern Africa's next crop is at risk from El Niño. Global grain supply is not disrupted.
rubric_hit: Watch: severe drought in major crop regions (East Africa, Sahel); no famine or major exporter harvest failure

sources.title: GEOGLAM Crop Monitor — Crop Monitor for Early Warning, No. 121 (November 2026)
Daily Maverick — El Niño threatens SA's crops but ample maize stocks cushion the blow

why: Drought slowly destroys harvests, hydropower and river shipping, and drives famine and migration.
drivers: Rainfall deficits, heat, ENSO, groundwater depletion.

rubric.alert: Drought driving famine conditions, a major exporter's harvest failure, or monsoon failure across a major breadbasket.
rubric.watch: Severe drought in a major crop region, a major river at record low, or a monsoon running more than 20% below normal.
rubric.normal: No major breadbasket in severe drought.
